rationale: bugs_open/315 fix candidate 4 / PLAN_2026-08-19 decision D5 — the last substantive item in that lane, and buildable for the first time today because the thing it compares against (pages.content_hash, RFC_038/DGH-013) only started being written on 2026-08-20. THE DEFECT: delivery on this estate is asynchronous and batched — a handler commits a page's file to the site repo ('commit is deploy') and a runner in the private gqls/sites repo b2-syncs the changed directory minutes later. Nothing on this side observes that sync, so a page can commit successfully, stamp deployed_at, report a COMPLETED orchestration, and never reach the origin. bugs_open/315's instance served its OLD render for about six hours through four completed rerenders with every internal signal green. The deep finding that reframed the bug was that the platform could not tell 'this page never needed republishing' from 'this page failed to republish' — identical in every signal it produced. WHY A HASH AND NOT A TIMESTAMP, and this is the hard constraint: the bug file's own candidate 4 proposed comparing deployed_at against the origin's last-modified. Run across 40 live pages on 2026-08-19 that returned 40 of 40 'stale', every one HEALTHY, persisting 85 minutes — because a byte-identical rerender legitimately rewrites nothing, so the origin's mtime says nothing about currency. Only a content hash separates the two cases. WHAT IT FINDS TODAY: nothing. Measured 2026-08-21, all 228 active pages then carrying a content_hash were fetched with a cache-buster and hashed: 228 of 228 MATCH across 12 domains. So this is a REGRESSION GUARD, the same posture as check_asset_reference_404 (96 of 96 assets serving 200 when it was written), and every branch is proven by an induced fault rather than by a live positive. That same sweep is also the end-to-end proof the comparison is sound: stored fingerprint and served bytes agree on 228 independent pages, so no encoding, transform or path-keying error sits between them.

plan.summary: Add one flag-only discovery check, page_content_divergence, that fetches each judgeable page with a unique cache-buster, sha256s the body, and compares it against pages.content_hash — filing a work item only on a confirmed, race-free mismatch, and retracting through CheckResult.Resolved on a positive re-observation. No handler agent in v1 (D5). No changes to any existing check, action or contract.

edits.rationale: NEW FILE, ~470 lines including the header. The check itself. Registered via init()->Register like every sibling; inert until a discovery agent names it in its checks array, and that config must NOT be applied before the image rolls because the runner hard-fails on an unregistered check name (the lesson migration 368 recorded for check_site_unreachable).
edits.sketch: Predicate (package-level const divergenceCandidatesQuery so a test can pin it): site_id=$1 AND p.status='active' (retracted/archived pages keep deployed_at BY DESIGN and are not served) AND p.content_hash IS NOT NULL (structurally inert without a fingerprint — 588 of 816 pages today, and it says nothing rather than guessing) AND p.deployed_at IS NOT NULL AND p.deployed_at < now() - make_interval(secs => $2). FIVE WAYS IT COULD LIE, EACH CLOSED IN CODE: (1) delivery in flight -> divergenceSettleWindow=30m; MEASURED 2026-08-21 over 1,099 readings / 85 pages / 95 deploy events, the only 3 DIVERGED readings were at ages 1s, 13s and 14s, all converged by 140-156s, and 0 of 995 readings at age>=157s diverged — so the window is ~128x the largest lag observed AND is load-bearing, because those 3 readings are 3 work items this check would otherwise have filed against healthy pages in 2h42m. (2) CDN edge -> every request carries a unique crypto/rand cache-buster; the 228-page proof used exactly this method fleet-wide. (3) page redeployed mid-probe (we read H1, a deploy writes H2 + new bytes, we convict H1) -> after a mismatch, contentIntentUnchanged() re-reads content_hash AND deployed_at and DISCARDS the candidate if either moved. (4) origin mid-write -> a mismatch is confirmed by a SECOND fetch and the two served hashes must AGREE; two different bodies is a moving target, logged, never filed. (5) a stale fingerprint written by nobody -> the stamp assigns content_hash only when the deploy-evidence guard RAN, so an UNARMED deployed-stamper would leave a hash describing an older deploy. MEASURED, not argued: exactly THREE live steps set status='deployed' via update_page_status (page-rerender/update_status, report-builder/update_status, section-editor/update_page_status) and ALL THREE declare deploy_result_field (migration 494). Zero unarmed stampers. That is a dependency on live config, NOT an invariant the code holds, and the header says so, names the re-runnable enumerating query, and points at PLAN D6 which proposes closing it at the stamp — deliberately NOT done here because it reverses a decision this council reviewed on 2026-08-19 and belongs in its own round. ONLY A 200 IS JUDGED: availability belongs to check_site_unreachable, which files on it and explicitly declines the staleness class ('mortgagecalculator serves a divergent render today — a staleness defect, not an availability one'), so the seam is clean and a non-200 here is a skip. Measured: 2 intermittent 404s appeared in the same watch, both serving one shared edge error page, each surrounded by MATCH — 2 more false items had they been judged as content. A body reaching divergenceMaxBodyBytes (8MB) is SKIPPED, never hashed, because sha256 over a truncated body is a different, confidently wrong answer. A url carrying a fragment or query is refused via the shared datahelpers.PageFilePathFromURL — the SAME definition that decided what to hash — because idea.uk has a live page at '/tools.html#audience-check' while a DIFFERENT page owns '/tools.html'. Per-pass cap 60 with the dropped urls LOGGED (webdesign.co.uk carries 124 hashed pages, so it bites). Emission: item_type page_content_divergence, severity high, priority 40, HandlerAgent DELIBERATELY EMPTY (D5 v1 flag-only — re-filing a rerender is the loop that already failed four times), ItemKey 'page_content_divergence:<page_id>' so a second pass re-files nothing, spec carries BOTH hashes in full so triage is a look. Retraction via CheckResult.Resolved on a positive match only — never inferred from absence.

edits.rationale: NEW FILE, 15 tests. The check has NO live positive (228 of 228 healthy), and 'it found nothing' is exactly what a silently broken check reports (016b §9). So the substitute is an induced fault per branch, actually RUN rather than intended.
edits.sketch: Network replaced at the same package-var seam check_asset_reference_404 uses (fetchServedPage), plus two tests against a real httptest server for the encoding question the seam cannot see. MUTATION TABLE, EVERY ROW EXECUTED 2026-08-21 (mutation applied to the real source, named test run, source restored byte-for-byte): drop the served-hash agreement -> OriginServingTwoBodiesFilesNothing FAILS; delete contentIntentUnchanged -> RedeployedDuringThePassFilesNothing FAILS; fetch a fragment url -> FragmentURLIsNeverFetched FAILS; drop the cache-buster -> EveryRequestCarriesAUniqueCacheBuster FAILS; add a handler_agent -> NeverRoutesToAHandler FAILS; stop retracting -> MatchingHashRetractsAndFilesNothing FAILS; raise the cap -> PerPassCapIsEnforced FAILS; drop status='active' -> QueryPinsItsFourGuards FAILS; set Accept-Encoding by hand -> FetchServedPageHashesTheDecodedBody FAILS. HONESTY ABOUT WHAT IS NOT PROVEN: the non-200 branch and the oversize branch each have a SECOND guard in series (the worker only fires a confirmation fetch for a judgeable 200), so deleting either ALONE changes no outcome and no test can be made to fail against it; the header says exactly that instead of claiming otherwise, and the DOUBLE mutation (branch + confirmation gate) does fail both named tests on their fetch-count assertions — measured. FOUR OF THESE ROWS WERE FALSE WHEN FIRST WRITTEN and the file records it: three tests passed against mutated source because a LATER guard absorbed the fault (an unscripted sqlmock query erroring; the confirmation gate), and the cap test sized its fixture AND its assertion from the very const under test, so raising the cap raised the expectation with it and the check silently widened. Each fixed at the test, with the fix noted where it lives.

edits.sketch: Adds "page_content_divergence": {catMechanical, "..."}. Classified on the way IN rather than waiting for a ratchet refresh (the mistyped_deployed_page / dark_section_audit precedent). Reason states: deliberately NOT a verifier candidate because verification would put an outbound HTTP probe on the COMPLETION path — the standing objection shared with asset_reference_404, image_url_404 and backend_entry_orphaned — and that it does not NEED one, being the posture contrast_failure moved to on 2026-08-12: the producer retracts its own findings on a positive re-observation, which is the same comparison a verifier would make, taken on the discovery path where the probe is already precedented. Also notes the item is flag-only, so nothing on the completion path claims it done in the first place. No other entry touched; the diff's other lines are gofmt realigning the adjacent block because the new key is longer.

plan.risks: ADDITIVE AND INERT ON APPLY. The check is registered but runs only when a discovery agent names 'page_content_divergence' in its checks array — no config change is in this submission, and the enabling migration must be held until the image carrying this file has rolled (StrictConfig/runner hard-fails on an unregistered check name). No existing check, action, contract or item type is modified; the only edit outside the two new files is one classification entry. WHAT COULD STILL GO WRONG, stated rather than left for the reviewer to find: (1) the stale-fingerprint case if a future agent adds an UNARMED update_page_status step — measured impossible today (3 of 3 armed), closed only by config discipline, with PLAN D6 proposing the structural fix at the stamp and deliberately not taking it here; (2) outbound HTTP volume — capped at 60 pages/site/pass with 4 workers and the dropped urls logged, against a fleet whose busiest site carries 124 hashed pages, so the cap DOES bite and says so; (3) flag-only means the items accumulate unless someone drains them — accepted for v1 per D5 and named as a cost, with retraction on positive re-observation keeping the queue self-clearing for anything that heals; (4) the 30-minute window means a genuine divergence is invisible for its first 30 minutes — a deliberate trade against 3 measured false positives, and the motivating six-hour case is still caught with hours to spare.
